sam.k: Quick Q  we just converted a long-term contractor to FTE with an effective date of Jan 15, approved today. Manager asked if we can backdate salary + benefits enrollment to Jan 15 and prorate sign-on. Payroll cutoff was yesterday.
people-ops: Congrats! Short answer: salary retro yes (next payroll) if backdate <= 90 days; benefits enrollment retro depends on carrier rules and open enrollment windows. For sign-on proration: comp-ops needs to confirm award and vesting treatment.
sam.k: Carrier told manager they can retro-enroll for 30 days only. What do we do if the carrier denies?
benefits-team: If carrier denies retro coverage, we can request a manual premium reimbursement for eligible medical costs during the gap, but need documented denial and employee receipts. Also verify benefit-eligible start date in HRIS matches payroll backdate.
comp-ops: For sign-on, if conversion triggers a one-time hiring bonus, comp-ops approves proration formula (we typically pro-rate by days in first 12 months). If equity is part of conversion, that's separate paperwork and may not be backdated.
sam.k: OK. For payroll submission, should I email payroll@ with the promo packet and benefits note? Anything special in subject?
payroll-bot: payroll-bot: Use subject: "Retro Conversion: [Last, First] - FTE Conversion - [Country]". Attach signed packet, HRIS start date, benefits carrier response (if any), payroll ID. Items after cutoff go to next run. Flag "PRORATE_SIGNON" if sign-on needs pro-rating.
people-ops: Checklist to send: 1) Signed conversion packet + Lattice link; 2) Effective/backdate date; 3) Payroll ID; 4) Benefits carrier confirmation or denial; 5) Comp-ops approval for sign-on proration.
sam.k: I'll gather docs and loop comp-ops + benefits. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
